the Kohn-Sham method and the CJT effective potential agree for the two halves, in both forms: for 80 states (two dimensions, two sets, two forms, strengths 1.5 and 3 times the respective binding threshold, total densities of the Fermi momenta 0.3 to 1.1 m; 40 with equal halves, 17 with unequal halves, 23 with one half filled) the stationary point of Omega(M_+, M_-, V_+, V_-; mu) at the chemical potential of the Kohn-Sham state, found by Newton's method from displaced start values, has the same two masses, the same density and energy density, and -Omega equals the Kohn-Sham pressure (sum of the deviations at most 4.9e-11; residuals of the four stationarity conditions at most 1.4e-12). In the states with unequal halves the two chemical potentials agree to 6.7e-16 (relative): the polarization is the equilibrium one. In all 23 states with one half filled the lowest state of the empty half lies above the chemical potential

the vacuum of the two forms with the filled states of negative energy (cutoff Lambda). The gap equations of the vacuum are (M_+ + M_-)/2 - m = G_Stot (s_+ + s_-) and (M_+ - M_-)/2 = G_Sdif (s_+ - s_-) with s_+- = -(NU/2) Int^Lambda M_+-/w. (a) Without mass term (m = 0) and for an attractive scalar coupling (sets A and B: G_S^HF < 0 < G_Sc) a field acquires a mass when |G_S^HF| exceeds the critical coupling |G_c| (D = 4: G_c Lambda^3 = -29.608813, D = 3: G_c Lambda^2 = -4.934802), in both forms at the same strength of the couplings: no mass 2 per cent below it, a mass 2 per cent above it. In the quantized-sector form the two halves acquire the SAME mass (M_+ = M_-: the mass term of the positive Lagrangian); in the covariant form they acquire masses of OPPOSITE sign (M_+ = -M_-: the mass term -m psitilde psi of the covariant Lagrangian), verified to 1e-7. (b) With the bare mass 0.05 Lambda the quantized-sector form passes smoothly through the critical strength (the two masses stay equal at all 101 clock readings), whereas the covariant form has a sharp transition at which the two masses separate: D = 4, set A: tau_d = 0.0091 (linear criterion 0.0091); D = 4, set B: tau_d = 0.0094 (linear criterion 0.0094); D = 3, set A: tau_d = 0.0194 (linear criterion 0.0194); D = 3, set B: tau_d = 0.0199 (linear criterion 0.0199); the strength of the transition agrees with the linear criterion 1 + G_Sdif NU Int^Lambda d^Dk/(2 pi)^D k^2/w^3 = 0 at the common mass to 2.1e-10
